_meta.title: Tag Lexicon — canonical tags, aliases, directives
_meta.purpose: THE tag vocabulary. Replaces the 9,557-line exhaustive variation list: instead of memorising every messy form, the engine runs the small generic normalisation pipeline in Tag_Normalisation_Spec.md against these aliases. Validated against the full historical corpus: 9,556/9,557 catalogued variations (99.99%) resolve correctly with these aliases + the pipeline rules; the single irreducible compound is in Tag_Exceptions.json.
_meta.how_matching_works: Aliases are matched case-, diacritic-, and whitespace-insensitively, after the mechanical normalisation steps (see spec): marker stripping, bracket repair, dash/quote folding, numbering removal. A single alias therefore covers hundreds of raw variations. Matching tries: exact -> colon-payload -> colon-head -> de-numbered -> embedded (longest alias at suffix > prefix > interior). Fragments are multi-matched (container + child), 'end X'/'/X' resolves generically to a CONTAINER_CLOSE of X, and fragments opening with an addressee prefix (CS/Dev/Note) are writer instructions and are never tag-matched.

directives.DROP: never emit (deliberate exclusion, e.g. sticky nav)

_meta.extension_rule: New writer phrasing for an existing tag = append ONE alias here. New tag = add ONE entry here. Never a code change.

condition_primary_demote._note: MODIFIER-NOT-PRIMARY fix (Chris). 'self check'/'autocheck' are aliases of 'typing quiz', so in a COMPOUND like [clickdrop quiz autocheck] the condition could win the primary slot over the real widget (click drop), building the wrong widget. When a span matches the listed tag VIA one of these condition aliases AND another non-condition INTERACTIVE tag is present, TagNormaliser demotes it so the real widget governs. A STANDALONE [self check]/[autocheck] (the only INTERACTIVE tag) is unaffected — it stays a typing/selfCheck widget. Env PRIMARYFIX_OFF reverts.

qualifier_alias_demote._note: QUALIFIER-NOT-CONTAINER fix (Chris, round 140, BLL241-01). The lone word 'interactive' is an alias of the 'activity' container, so a QUALIFIER span like [Interactive Stop Watch] / [interactive tool] / [interactive stopwatch] / lone [Interactive] resolves to an [activity] CONTAINER_OPEN and mis-opens a NUMBERLESS activity box that SPLITS the real activity (BLL241 1C: the audio + drag-words fell out of the box into a second, unnamed box). Genuine containers ALWAYS carry the word 'activity' ([interactive activity] ×57, which yields a SEPARATE alias:'activity' tag). So: when the resolved PRIMARY is an 'activity' CONTAINER_OPEN whose alias is a listed qualifier AND there is NO other 'activity' tag from a non-qualifier alias, TagNormaliser DROPS the qualifier-only activity tag → the span falls through to instruction/noise and no longer opens/splits a box. A widget-primary span ([Interactive – drag and drop] → drag and drop) is untouched (activity is never the primary there). Env INTERACTIVEQUAL_OFF reverts.
qualifier_alias_demote._round217_note: ROUND 217 (Chris, boundary audit — AGH1001-01). standalone_becomes: a BARE standalone '[Interactive]' span (the demoted alias is the span's ONLY tag, matched EXACTLY) is the writer's generic widget INVOCATION, not a qualifier — it is re-tagged as this generic INTERACTIVE opener (canonical 'interactive'; no lexicon tags entry needed — GetWidgetTypes returns [] so the scanner types the bundle 'unclassified', and the round-217 activity_wrapper.standalone_widget_box then wraps it in the human's `activity interactive` box). Embedded qualifier forms ('[Interactive Stop Watch]') and multi-tag spans still demote-drop exactly as before. Measured 13 bare spans / 8 modules (AGH1001 x5). Env INTALIAS_OFF reverts the bare form to the plain demote (pre-217: instruction class, no bundle, the following data table leaking as a kept <table>).

tag_promote._note: ELEMENT->CONTAINER promote (Chris, round 170, ENGS102-1.0 screenshot review). A resolved ELEMENT tag whose HUMAN rendering is really a different CONTAINER convention is promoted to that container tag so its existing machinery fires. Rules today: [Supervisor button] -> [Supervisor note] (round 170), and the round-239 [right-hand alert] -> [side alert] (Dev-Feedback R2/B1: a rule may carry when_match, a regex tested against the span's FOLDED text — the promote then fires only when the span matches, so a broad 'from' tag like the generic 'alert' can be promoted for ONE spelling only). The writer's supervisor side-note is authored as a green 'button' in the WT, but the human developer renders it as the SAME super-content reveal PANEL it builds for [Supervisor note] (measured 17/19 [supervisor button] modules build the panel; probe outputs/_measure_supnote_separation.py). Promoting the resolved tag+directive routes [Supervisor button] through the whole round-143/160/162/163 supervisor-panel pipeline (scan / pair / activity-lookahead / callouts.by_tag all key on primary.tag === 'supervisor note'). Applied in TagNormaliser.Parse AFTER the primary is chosen; every matching tag in the span is rewritten (tag + directive) and the primary recomputed. Per-rule env toggle. NOTE this only rehomes the SEQUENTIAL (standalone) supervisor-button cases; a supervisor-button sitting in a 2-cell content|note LAYOUT table (the ENG family) is a separate table-composition follow-up.

rules._doc: ROUND 239 (Dev-Feedback R2, B1 — SCCH302-01). The writer's [right-hand alert] is the side tip-box the human ships as an alertActivity col-md-4 RIGHT column paired with the preceding content column (the r121/r123 side-alert machinery), but the bracket fell through to the generic 'alert' substring -> a full-width plain alert with the content as a lead paragraph + a stray empty row>col-12. Promoting the resolved 'alert' to 'side alert' (ONLY when the folded span matches right[- ]hand alert — measured corpus population of that exact spelling: ZERO modules, SCCH302 the first; the wider RHS-alert phrasing family ([rhs alert] x31, [alert box right hand side] etc — 80 occ / 40 modules, all shipped as plain alerts today) is RECORDED as its own follow-up round, not silently rerouted here) routes it through the whole existing side-alert pipeline. Env RHSALERT_OFF reverts to the plain-alert render.

ROUND 304 (the orphan-remaining chain, round 3 of 4) — THE LESSON-SUMMARY BOX. A writer ends a lesson with [summary box] and the module's summary run beneath it; 'box' is an alias of the widget sub-part `shape n`, whose directive is SUBTAG, so the marker reached the ORPHAN branch, printed 'Red Flag: Orphan sub-tag [shape n] outside an interactive' and the summary shipped as loose paragraphs with a red flag over them. The human developer boxes it. Promoting the resolved tag to `alert` routes it through the WHOLE existing callout pipeline (the r105 strict containment, the content_wrap row>col-12, and — the piece that makes the PLACEMENT right — container_auto_close.activity_close_before, which already lists CONTAINER_OPEN, so an activity still open at the marker is closed first and the box lands in its OWN section row, which is where the gold puts it 27 times out of 29). MEASURED PER WRITER FORM against the human's own page (outputs/_measure_r304_box.cjs + _r304_analyse.py): [summary box] is boxed on 28 of 28 judgeable pages = 100%, and it is the ONLY form in this family that behaves consistently — [coloured box] is boxed 10 of 15 = 67% and the plain [Box] form 0 of 10 (ENGR202's gold builds an ACCORDION from it) — so the catalogue's '94.7% agreement, ~120 flags' is an average over three populations that disagree, and BOTH other forms are MEASURED DECLINES rather than deferred work. THE CLASS IS EDITORIAL, not derivable: alert 18 / alert solid 10 over that population, with EVERY module internally pure (XMES203/XTAS101/XTAS102/XTAS103/XLP02/XLP04 alert; XMES201/XMES202/XDLS912 alert solid) and no signal whatever in the writer's document — the r200 videoSection-icon situation. `alert` is the 0.64 majority (0.67 by module), above the r182 solidify floor and not a tie, so it ships as the corpus form and the three solid modules are NAMED divergences, never chased. THE HEADING IS ALSO EDITORIAL and is deliberately NOT promoted: the gold heads the box

18 times and leaves it plain 10, the colon-versus-full-stop discriminator is only 0.67 and splits by module too, and 5 of the 18 headings are in NO writer text at all — a heading is never invented (the r303 rule), so the writer's own first line ships as the

the gold uses on XTAS101/102/103. clear_remainder is load-bearing: without it the leftover word 'summary' maps through callouts.modifier_classes to class='alert summary', a class the gold library never uses.

mtk_quiz_retag._note: ROUND 232 (Change Ledger CL-0038, 16 Jul — Chris). Any [MTKquiz]-family span (any modifiers) ships the canonical 'Go to quiz' button + a Designer/Developer To Do note; the writer's quiz content stays rendered; the 'dropbox' wrapper modifier does NOT attach. The family's live resolutions were all over the map (measured, outputs/_detect_mtkquiz.cjs — 33 spans / 21 modules): most forms hit mcq INTERACTIVE via the embedded 'quiz' alias (an un-built bundle that swallowed the writer's quiz content into a placeholder dump), [MTKQuiz]/[Auto-marked MTKquiz] were bare instructions, the 'Free text box…' form mis-resolved to a text box ELEMENT and the 'teacher dropbox' form to dropdown. This span-level RETAG (applied in TagNormaliser.Parse after tag_promote, and ALSO on tag-less instruction spans) normalises them all: quiz-junk tags in drop_tags are removed, ONE 'mtk quiz' ELEMENT tag is injected, and the primary is recomputed SURVIVORS-FIRST (a surviving [Activity]/[drag and drop] co-tag keeps governing — [Activity 1A: MTK Quiz] still opens its box; only when the old primary was dropped or null does mtk quiz take the slot). head_pattern matches the family head (MTKQuiz/MTK Quiz/MTK-quiz); exclude_pattern keeps the ARFUN01 closer ([End of MTK Quiz content] stays a CONTAINER_CLOSE, never a button); bracketless_max_words caps the bracket-less red-line form (ENG1004/ENG1005 'Activity – long answer MTK quiz, Kaiako marked', measured the ONLY bracket-less carriers corpus-wide) so a long prose note mentioning an MTK quiz can never retag. Emit templates + the adjacent writer-button absorb live in Emit_Templates.interactive_builders.mtk_quiz. Env MTKQUIZ_OFF reverts the whole family to the measured pre-round behaviour.

unresolved_marker_retag._note: ROUND 266 (CHFUN01, 'SEPARATE UNBUILT INTERACTIVE'). A span that resolved NO tags at all but opens with a known quiz-family marker is RETAGGED as the listed canonical INTERACTIVE, so the writer's quiz opens its own bundle (an honest hand-off box) instead of leaking as an instruction note + loose body text. CONTAINMENT BY CONSTRUCTION: only zero-tag spans are touched — every span that already resolves anything ([dropquiz][autocheck] -> typing quiz on ~8 modules) is byte-unchanged. Measured live over all corpus WTs (the dropquiz census, r266): the zero-tag population is CHFUN01/04, HPRE203 x2, OSAI501, OSGM301, OSGM501, OSOH101, OSSM301 — their golds build dropDown/mcq quizzes at those spots. Env toggle: DROPQUIZ_OFF.

side alert._doc: ROUND 121 (Chris, BLL210) — a `[Side alert]` is the writer's SIDE tip-box that the human renders as `<div class="alertActivity">` in a narrow side column (col-md-4/3), NOT the generic `[alert]` box (which Claude was emitting via the bare 'alert' substring match). Distinct canonical so callouts.by_tag routes it to the alertActivity shape. 43 modules / 100 human alertActivity elements; Claude built 0.

hint._note: ROUND 65+ (Chris): split out from 'hint slider' — a bare [hint] is the simple click-to-reveal hint (catalogue #25), NOT the multi-row hint slider (#26). ROUND 277 CORRECTION: the old claim that 'a single hint = a one-row slider, so no build is lost' was WRONG in both halves. They are different ELEMENTS in the gold — hint is p.hintLink + span.hint + div.hintDropContent, hintSlider is div.hintSlider > hintRow > frontInfo|backInfo — and dispatching the hint widget_type at the shared builder lost EVERY build, because Emit_Templates.interactive_builders had no 'hint' key, so Build returned null at its missing-template guard before any builder ran (0 of 64 built). Both types now enter InteractiveBuilder#hintEntry, which routes on the authored CONTENT rather than the tag: the tag is not a reliable discriminator ([hint sliders] resolves here, to widget_type hint, yet IS a slider; OSAI401/501 author sliders under [hint slider]). Reverts by data (re-add 'hint' to the hint slider aliases); env HINTELEM_OFF restores the pre-277 no-build state.

mtk quiz._note: ROUND 232 (CL-0038): the canonical MTK-quiz marker — renders as the 'Go to quiz' button + Designer/Developer To Do note (templates in Emit_Templates.interactive_builders.mtk_quiz). DELIBERATELY NO ALIASES: natural alias matching is not env-gateable, so the span-level retag in _meta.mtk_quiz_retag (env MTKQUIZ_OFF) does ALL the matching; this entry is the taxonomy record + directive lookup for the injected tag.

embed.aliases_note: ROUND NN (Chris, ENGS302): 'imbed' is a recurrent writer misspelling of 'embed'; '[Imbed film]'/'[imbed film]' previously resolved to null (neither 'imbed' nor 'film' was an alias) and the whole tag leaked. 'imbed video'/'Imbed video' still resolve to VIDEO (the 'video' suffix wins over the 'imbed' prefix); a video-host '[Imbed film]' now reaches the embed branch which routes YouTube/Vimeo to the videoSection video builder.

end other._suffix_close_note: SUFFIX CLOSE FORMS (2026-06-15, over-capture #3): writers close a widget with '[Carousel ends here]'/'[accordion ends]'/'[modal ends]' as often as the prefix '[End carousel]' (measured 100+ corpus occurrences). Without these the embedded widget name ('carousel') matched first → the marker OPENED a new empty widget AND failed to close the open one (ENGJ301 had 8 '[Carousel ends here]'). Listed here as CONTAINER_CLOSE; the scanner now terminates an open widget on ANY CONTAINER_CLOSE directive. 'coloured box ends' = a callout close, harmless as a widget terminator too.
